data.narrative:
Cognition is a Series A-stage AI & Software company founded by Scott Wu, Steven Hao, and Walden Yan that has raised $400M+. The valuation analysis draws on a comparison universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Palantir), including stage-adjacent companies such as Scale AI, Reflection AI, Physical Intelligence, and Black Forest Labs.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $1.0B total-raised proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implies a valuation of $2.0B. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $15.3B, with a range spanning $3.2B (Black Forest Labs, Series B) to $29.0B (Scale AI, Series B). The dispersion reflects both stage variation within the peer set and heterogeneity in investor appetite for frontier AI infrastructure.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $1.7B (low) to $17.6B (high), with a median of $8.7B. The wide band reflects material uncertainty around Cognition's current revenue run-rate, product-market fit trajectory, and the comparability of peer valuations in a market segment characterized by rapid repricing. Stage-progression methodology yields the lower bound; peer benchmarking yields the upper. Resolution of this range hinges on revenue visibility and customer concentration metrics not available in current data.
